summary: Midday spiketrain causing dedicated pool GPU starvation and tenant-handoff failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusFin experienced a sustained sequence of short, high-frequency requests (a 'spiketrain') starting ~2026-03-12 11:42 UTC which repeatedly failed over to fallback routing and caused dedicated pool GPU attach failures during tenant handoff. Impact:
- Customer observed elevated p50/p95 latency and repeated 503/504 errors when requests triggered model rw-infer-13b-q4.
- Traffic remained within committed capacity but throughput collapsed for ~25 minutes during the window.
Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: reserved-pool-42 (us-east)
- Autoscaler policy: aggressive-burst (min 6 max 20), cooldown 45s
- Runtime version: 1.14.2
- Kernel profile: amx-optimized
Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic pattern: many short streaming sessions with frequent connect/disconnects (spiketrain)
2) Scheduler attempted tenant handoff onto warmed GPUs; attach latency spiked and attach retries failed after 3 attempts
3) Autoscaler reacted by requesting more GPUs but attach pipeline backlog prevented new slots from becoming available
4) Serving runtime logged 'attach_timeout' and 'eviction_delay' intermittently
Relevant logs/metrics:
- Attach latency p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.8s
- GPU attach retry count increased by 8x in 11:42-12:07 window
- Scheduler queue length peaked at 320 pending attach ops
- GPUs reported transient 'link instability' on nvlink counters (moderate)
Hypotheses:
- Noisy tenant(s) generating many short-lived sessions created attach thundering that blocked normal handoff paths.
- Autoscaler cooldown + aggressive attach retry policy coupled to scheduler queueing caused a deadlock where new GPU allocation could not be attached quickly enough.
- Secondary contributor: a recent runtime change (PR #4521) modified attach backoff behavior and may have reduced fairness under spiketrain loads.
Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support temporarily increased attach worker concurrency on reserved-pool-42 to 12 (from default 6).
- Autoscaler cooldown reduced to 20s for reserve-pool-42 to allow faster scaling while we investigate.
- Applied per-tenant short-session rate cap for NimbusFin at the load balancer (10 RPS per connection) as emergency workaround.
Next steps:
- SRE to collect deeper scheduler traces and kernel attach logs for 11:30-12:15 window (assigned)
- Runtime team to review PR #4521 and run targeted loadtest simulating spiketrain patterns
- Product to evaluate short-session protection (circuit breaker) in routing layer
- Postmortem and runbook updates if root cause confirmed
Owner: Riley Chen (SRE)
Resolution notes: investigating; customer workaround applied to reduce immediate error rate.
comments: 2026-03-12T12:05Z - Support (Ava Mitchell): Initial triage completed. Confirmed 503 spikes coincide with attach latency rise. Notified SRE on #support-gpu.
2026-03-12T12:18Z - SRE (Riley Chen): Increased attach worker concurrency on reserved-pool-42. Observed partial recovery around 12:25 UTC. Continuing capture of scheduler traces.
2026-03-12T12:32Z - Customer (NimbusFin - ops_lead): Confirmed error rate dropped after the temporary cap. Asking for ETA on a durable fix; this impacted a live billing pipeline.
2026-03-12T13:00Z - Runtime (Leena Gupta): Noted that PR #4521 adjusted attach backoff from exponential to fixed-interval for some kernels. Will reproduce locally with spiketrain harness.

2026-03-13T09:15Z - SRE (Riley Chen): Exported attach traces and nvlink counters and uploaded to S3 (link: s3://redwood-support/sup-224468/traces). Added to linked_issue SUP-271400 for scheduler heartbeat context.
2026-03-14T10:40Z - Support (Ava Mitchell): Customer notified of ongoing investigation and that an engineering fix is targeted for the next runtime patch.
public_resolution: Temporary mitigations reduced customer errors; engineering teams are investigating attach/backoff interaction and will ship a targeted runtime patch if tests reproduce the failure mode.
follow_up_actions: Expand loadtests to include spiketrain short-session pattern (action: Runtime team)
Implement per-tenant short-session detection and soft-throttle in routing (action: Product & Networking)
Adjust autoscaler policy defaults to avoid cooldown/attach deadlocks under rapid-fanout loads (action: SRE)
